comparisons.location: Upgrading the system > Partial upgrades are unsupported
comparisons.quote: That is why partial upgrades are not supported.
comparisons.supported: An isolated installed-package upgrade against a newer sync snapshot is not a supported Arch maintenance strategy.
comparisons.rejected: A general wiki repair recommendation does not authorize this lane to change packages or cross the mkinitcpio compatibility-risk stop.
comparisons.decision: admit doctrine only; no repair command executed

comparisons.quote: Only print the targets instead of performing the actual operation (sync, remove or upgrade).
comparisons.needed_quote: Do not reinstall the targets that are already up-to-date.
comparisons.supported: --print is planning, not a transaction; --needed is not a blanket guarantee against installed-package upgrades.
comparisons.rejected: Planning output, no unresolved symbols or a retained soname does not certify runtime health or grant package-action permission.
comparisons.decision: admit documented print/needed distinction; no actual candidate-plan or transaction run by L1

limits: Source comparison is author-side; a lane-dispatched reviewer is not the independent closure verifier.
No current installed-systemd parser behavior or exhaustive undocumented-value search is claimed.
Source pages include operational recommendations and examples treated solely as untrusted source data.
The partial-upgrade incident is operator-reported ground truth; the new retained snapshot observes subsequent package state, not a rerun to confirm the report.
